THE SCHOOL HALL · THANKSGIVING · AGES 2–5

Thanksgiving — what it is and how little kids celebrate.

Thanksgiving is the thank-you holiday: a big dinner, a full table and everyone naming what they are thankful for.

Back to the Hall ↗
WHAT IS THANKSGIVING?

What’s this? Why do we celebrate it?

Thanksgiving comes on the fourth Thursday of November, and its whole idea fits in one small word: thanks. Long ago, families who had worked hard in the fields all year gathered everything they had grown — corn, pumpkins, bread — and cooked a giant dinner to share with their neighbors. They were thankful for the food and for each other. Today families still do exactly that: they travel, they cook together, they sit down at a big table, and before eating, everyone takes a turn saying one thing they are thankful for.

For a little kid, Thanksgiving is easy to understand: it is the day we say thank you out loud, to the people who feed us, love us and help us grow.

TRY IT · ACTIVITIES FOR KIDS

Little hands at the thank-you table.

Trace your child’s hand on paper — the palm becomes a turkey body, the fingers become feathers, and on every feather someone writes one thankful thing. Make a thankful tree: cut paper leaves and add one each day of November. Let your child set the table (plates, cups, spoons — the Sequence Stories card knows the order) and fold the napkins any way they like. Ask the dinnertime question together: “What made you smile today?” That is a thank-you, too.
